instructions: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows. Pause briefly near the bottom, then press through your palms to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out. Brace your core and push your hips back as if sitting into a chair. Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as low as comfortable. Drive through your heels to stand back up. Keep your chest up throughout the movement.

Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under shoulders and extend your legs behind you. Keep your body in a straight line and engage your core. Avoid letting your hips sag or pike upward. Hold the position for the target duration while breathing steadily.

Stand upright with feet together and arms at your sides. Jump your feet out while simultaneously raising your arms overhead. Jump back to the starting position. Continue at a steady pace for the desired duration.

muscle_groups_activated: Chest, Shoulders, Triceps, Quadriceps, Core, Glutes
instructions: Stand tall, then squat down and place your hands on the floor. Kick your feet back into a plank position. Perform a push-up if desired, then jump your feet back toward your hands. Explode upward into a jump with arms overhead. Repeat smoothly.

Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Step forward with one leg and lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees are bent about 90 degrees. Push through the front heel to bring the back leg forward into the next lunge step. Alternate legs as you move forward.

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart. Engage your core and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips toward the ceiling. Pause at the top with your body in a straight line from shoulders to knees. Lower under control and repeat.

Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs in a running motion. Keep your hips level and core tight. Continue alternating at a controlled but brisk pace.

Use parallel bars, a bench, or a sturdy elevated surface. Support your body with straight arms and shoulders down. Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Press back up to the starting position without locking out harshly.

Lie on one side and place your forearm on the floor with elbow under shoulder. Stack your feet or place one foot in front of the other for stability. Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet. Hold while keeping your core engaged, then switch sides.

Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells at chest level with palms facing forward. Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are extended without locking out aggressively. Lower them slowly until your elbows are just below the bench level. Repeat with controlled form.

Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height and palms facing forward. Brace your core and press the weights overhead until your arms are extended. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level with control. Avoid arching your lower back.

muscle_groups_activated: Lats, Rhomboids, Traps, Biceps, Rear Delts
instructions: Hinge at the hips with a flat back and hold dumbbells beneath your shoulders. Pull the weights toward your torso by driving your elbows back. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top. Lower the dumbbells slowly and repeat.

Hold one dumbbell vertically at chest height with both hands. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and sit back into a squat while keeping your chest up. Descend until your elbows come close to the inside of your knees or your depth limit. Drive through your heels to stand.

Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides and palms facing forward. Keep your elbows close to your body as you curl the weights toward your shoulders. Pause briefly at the top and lower them under control. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

Stand with dumbbells at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows. Raise the weights out to the sides until they reach shoulder height. Lower slowly with control. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging.

Stand holding a barbell at hip level with feet about hip-width apart. Keep a slight bend in the knees and hinge at the hips as you lower the bar along your thighs. Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings while keeping your back flat. Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

muscle_groups_activated: Quadriceps, Glutes, Hamstrings, Core, Lower Back
instructions: Place a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Brace your core, sit back and down, and lower until your hips reach appropriate depth. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes. Press through your heels to stand back up.

Lie on a bench with eyes under the bar and feet planted on the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it. Lower the bar to mid-chest with control, then press it back up until arms are extended. Keep your shoulder blades squeezed together throughout.

Stand with the barbell at shoulder height and hands just outside shoulder width. Tighten your core and press the bar overhead in a straight line. Move your head slightly back as the bar passes your face, then bring it under the bar at lockout. Lower back to the shoulders with control.

muscle_groups_activated: Glutes, Hamstrings, Erector Spinae, Lats, Forearms, Core
instructions: Stand with the bar over midfoot and hinge down to grip it with a flat back. Brace your core, push the floor away, and lift the bar by extending your hips and knees together. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout the lift. Return it to the floor with control by hinging at the hips.

muscle_groups_activated: Glutes, Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Shoulders, Traps, Core
instructions: Stand holding a barbell at thigh level with a shoulder-width grip. Hinge slightly, then explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar upward. Quickly pull yourself under the bar and catch it at the shoulders in a front rack position. Stand tall to finish the rep.

Sit in the leg press machine with your back and head supported on the pad. Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform and release the safety handles. Lower the platform by bending your knees until they reach a comfortable depth. Press through your feet to extend your legs without locking out forcefully.

Sit at the lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pads. Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width and pull it down toward your upper chest. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back, then slowly return the bar to the top. Avoid leaning back excessively or jerking the weight.

muscle_groups_activated: Lats, Rhomboids, Traps, Biceps, Rear Delts
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with feet braced and hold the handle with arms extended. Keep your chest tall and pull the handle toward your torso by driving your elbows back. Squeeze your back muscles at the end of the pull. Extend your arms forward slowly and repeat.

Adjust the seat so the handles are aligned with mid-chest. Sit with your back flat against the pad and press the handles forward until your arms are nearly extended. Return the handles slowly until your elbows are just behind your torso. Keep your shoulders down and stable.

Sit on the machine with your knees aligned with the pivot point. Place your ankles behind the padded roller and grip the handles. Extend your legs until they are nearly straight, then lower the weight under control. Avoid swinging or lifting your hips off the seat.

Position yourself on the hamstring curl machine so the roller pad rests comfortably above your ankles or behind your legs depending on the machine type. Curl the weight by bending your knees and bringing the pad toward your glutes. Pause briefly, then lower slowly. Keep your hips pressed into the pad.

Sit with your back against the pad and forearms or hands placed on the machine arms. Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a controlled arc. Squeeze your chest at the midpoint, then return slowly until you feel a stretch. Keep your shoulders down and avoid bouncing.

Sit with your back supported and the handles positioned at shoulder height. Press the handles upward until your arms are extended comfortably. Lower the weight back down with control to the starting position. Keep your core engaged and avoid arching your back.

Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar or rope attached at the high pulley. Keep your elbows tucked to your sides and push the handle downward until your arms are fully extended. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, then return slowly until your forearms are about parallel to the floor. Avoid letting your elbows drift forward.

muscle_groups_activated: Rear Delts, Traps, Rhomboids, Rotator Cuff
instructions: Set a rope attachment at upper-chest or face height. Pull the rope toward your face while flaring your elbows out and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause at the end of the movement, then return the rope under control. Keep your torso stable and avoid using momentum.

Attach a handle to a cable machine and stand sideways to the stack. With arms extended or slightly bent, pull the cable diagonally across your body in a chopping motion. Rotate through your torso and hips in a controlled manner. Return slowly to the start and repeat on both sides.

muscle_groups_activated: Lats, Biceps, Rhomboids, Rear Delts, Core
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Engage your core and pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down. Lower yourself with control until your arms are fully extended. Use assistance if needed to maintain good form.

Hang from a bar with palms facing toward you and hands about shoulder-width apart. Pull your body upward until your chin clears the bar. Lower slowly back to a full hang. Keep your body controlled and avoid swinging.

Hang from a pull-up bar with your body steady and shoulders engaged. Keeping your legs together, raise them forward until they are at hip height or higher as mobility allows. Lower them slowly without swinging. Maintain tension in your core throughout.

Kneel on the floor holding an ab wheel with both hands. Brace your core and roll the wheel forward slowly, keeping your hips from collapsing. Extend as far as you can while maintaining control, then pull back to the starting position using your core and shoulders. Avoid arching your lower back.

Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width and hold a kettlebell with both hands. Hinge at the hips and swing the kettlebell back between your legs. Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the bell up to chest height. Let the kettlebell return by hinging again, not by squatting deeply.

Hold a kettlebell close to your chest with both hands. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a squat while keeping your torso upright. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive up through your feet to stand. Keep the weight stable against your body.

Stand in front of a sturdy bench or box. Place one foot fully on the elevated surface and drive through that heel to lift your body up. Bring the other foot onto the box, then step back down with control. Alternate leading legs for each rep or set.

Stand upright with feet about hip-width apart. Rise onto the balls of your feet by lifting your heels as high as possible. Pause briefly at the top, then lower your heels slowly back to the floor. Use a wall or support for balance if needed.

Hinge at the hips with a flat back and hold dumbbells beneath your chest. With a slight bend in the elbows, raise the weights out to the sides until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower slowly. Keep the movement controlled and avoid swinging.

Set one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or corner. Hold the free end at shoulder height with both hands or one hand. Press the bar upward and forward in an arc until the arm or arms are extended. Lower slowly and keep your torso braced.

Sit at a preacher bench and place your upper arms against the pad. Grip the bar with an underhand hold and curl it toward your shoulders. Lower the bar slowly until your arms are nearly straight. Keep your upper arms in contact with the pad throughout the set.

Sit or stand in the calf raise machine depending on the equipment style. Position the balls of your feet on the platform and allow your heels to lower for a full stretch. Raise your heels as high as possible by contracting your calves. Pause at the top and lower under control.

Adjust the back extension bench so your hips are supported and your upper body can hinge freely. Cross your arms or hold a plate at your chest. Lower your torso by hinging at the hips, then raise it until your body is in a straight line. Avoid hyperextending the lower back at the top.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a medicine ball overhead. Engage your core and forcefully slam the ball into the floor. Squat down to pick it up with a flat back and repeat. Use a ball appropriate for your strength level and space.

Hold one end of a battle rope in each hand and stand in an athletic stance. Create alternating or simultaneous waves by moving your arms rapidly while keeping your core tight. Maintain a slight bend in your knees and stable posture. Continue for the target interval.

muscle_groups_activated: Quadriceps, Glutes, Hamstrings, Calves, Shoulders, Core
instructions: Place both hands on the sled handles with your body leaning forward. Drive one leg at a time to push the sled across the floor or turf. Keep your torso rigid and take powerful, short steps. Continue for the set distance or time.

Hold the handles with elbows close to your sides and the rope behind your heels. Rotate the rope with your wrists and hop lightly as it passes under your feet. Keep jumps low and land softly on the balls of your feet. Maintain a steady rhythm for the desired duration.
